about: The HJW Vineyard is where it all began. Hermann J. Wiemer, who learned to graft Mosel Riesling as a boy in Bernkastel, planted these slopes above Seneca Lake’s west shore between 1976 and 1978. They were among the first successful vinifera plantings in the Finger Lakes. The winery he founded in 1979 is now run by his apprentice Fred Merwarth and partner Oskar Bynke, and it bottles this original site on its own as a single-vineyard wine.

The 2023 is the first vintage of this wine from fully Demeter-certified biodynamic vines, the result of two decades of herbicide-free farming with cover crops, livestock and biodynamic preparations. The grapes were hand picked in two passes and sorted by hand. They were pressed as whole clusters, fermented with native yeasts, then aged six months in stainless steel. The wine finished with just under seven grams of residual sugar, balanced by the vineyard’s firm acidity.

Critics have rated it among the finest wines of the region. James Suckling gave it 96 points and praised its depth and intensity of fruit. Vinous called it the place “where Finger Lakes Riesling shines.” Wine Advocate gave it 92+. Expect layers of citrus, white peach and tropical fruit over bright acidity and a clean mineral finish, with the chalk and crushed-stone notes that critics often find in this site.
